- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is trending down, avoid overcorrecting; maintain slight upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (prices oscillating near 65–70), model should not overreact to recent spikes; dampen momentum.  
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift: reduce forecast slope if sentiment turns negative, increase if turning positive.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon, apply a 3–5% downward bias to early period.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.8) and price is trending sideways, forecast should reflect consolidation, not sharp moves — avoid predicting 3–5% swings without clear signal.
